content.question: Why is K-fold cross-validation generally faster than leave-p-out cross-validation?
options: Because K-fold reuses the same fitted model across all folds instead of retraining it.
Because K-fold fits the model K times, while leave-p-out needs to fit it far more often.
Because leave-p-out must run a full hyperparameter search for every possible train–test split.
Because K-fold scores the model on fewer data points, so validation itself is much cheaper.
content.answer: Because K-fold fits the model K times, while leave-p-out needs to fit it far more often.
